scope: Default-visible deterministic tests drive the concrete production realtime cycle runner through real loopback TLS and the production watcher supervisor. They cover disconnect, rate limiting, fragmented successful polling, bounded retry reset, cancellation during backoff, and permanent authentication rejection.

tests.name: realtime::tests::l010_tls_tests::real_tls_provider_failures_flow_through_the_production_watcher_without_a_storm
tests.coverage: An accepted IDLE session disconnects, two provider LIMIT failures produce first and second bounded delays, a fragmented polling session succeeds, the next failure resets to the first delay, and cancellation while that delay is held prevents a fifth TCP accept.

tests.name: realtime::tests::l010_tls_tests::real_tls_authentication_rejection_pauses_the_production_watcher_without_reconnect
tests.coverage: A real TLS IMAP LOGIN rejection publishes paused authentication state, requests no retry delay, and opens no second provider connection.

featureIsolation.trustBoundary: The fixture accepts only its exact loopback endpoint, exact fictional account identity, sentinel-owned temporary root, and CA file inside that root. Each wrapper runs its fixture environment in an isolated child process. Production certificate verification remains mandatory.

harnessHardening.exactChildProof: A successful isolated child must report running exactly one test, the exact requested test name ending in ok, and one passed with zero failed. Rust test status alone is insufficient because an exact filter matching zero tests exits successfully.
harnessHardening.timeout: The asynchronous child process has a 10 second hard timeout and kill-on-drop enabled.
harnessHardening.environmentRestoration: All seven fixture environment variables are restored through a panic-safe RAII guard inside the isolated process.

findingsFixed: A zero-test isolated child could previously exit successfully.
The isolated child previously had no hard timeout.
independentReview.finalResult: No remaining material issue in this slice. The reviewer independently reran both focused TLS tests successfully.

limitations: The user declined a physical sleep and wake interruption, so physical wake recovery remains an explicit waiver rather than a pass.
These deterministic source tests prove bounded supervisor ordering and cancellation, not native UI frame latency, memory growth, socket counts, or long-duration soak performance.
Native measured performance and the coordinated final full-source baseline remain separate evidence lanes.
